source: docs/work-orders/009-combat-model.md (including 'Settled after the first draft'); docs/work-orders/011-rustmoor-combat-stats.md ('Settled after the first draft' and 'Settled after the inspector's review'); docs/gdd.md sections 1, 6 (Combat paragraph), 7; content/monsters/rustmoor.json; content/tuning/xp-curve.json; docs/work-orders/001-xp-curve.md and 008-rustmoor-drops.md (carried-forward notes); docs/work-orders/012-rustmoor-cooking.md (the Rustmoor Ration, revision 5; 'Settled after review', revision 6); docs/work-orders/013-grocer-and-starting-inventory.md (the Ration consumption correction, revision 7); docs/work-orders/025-scrapjaw-on-day-14.md (Scrapjaw's reference weapon, revision 8); docs/work-orders/028-tailoring-and-first-armour.md (armour points at +0, revision 9)
applies_to: every fight: the seven combat skills, weapons and armour, monsters and bosses in all zones

basis_key.settled: Jeremy has decided it (work order 009, 'Settled after the first draft', 22 October 2026); where the GDD records it, the line is quoted
basis_key.derived: follows from a quoted GDD line or an existing approved file; the derivation names it
basis_key.proposal: a choice made here for Jeremy to accept or change; not canon
basis_key.open: the model needs it but neither the GDD nor a derivation gives it; value is null and the work order that will set it is named

units.settled: Work order 009: 'Hit points and damage are scaled x10, so the engine rolls whole numbers.'
units.rule: Every hit point and damage quantity (max HP, monster HP, max hits, swing damage, DPS, Ration heal) is ten times its revision-1 value. Times, probabilities, multipliers, levels, accuracy, evasion and armour are not HP or damage and are unchanged. Every kill time, Ration count per kill, damage share and win chance is a ratio of two scaled quantities, so all are unchanged from revision 1.
units.whole_number_rolls: The engine rolls whole numbers of damage; how it rounds is the engine's own concern, not part of this model. Checks use the closed forms below as written, with continuous moments. At x10 scale rounding a roll moves a swing's mean by at most 0.5 HP.

closed_forms_for_checks.settled: Work order 009, settled with revision 2: 'Checks use the closed forms as written (continuous moments); the engine's whole-number rolls are its own concern.'

PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S.note: One swing every 3 s for every style and weapon. Weapons do not carry their own interval, to keep gear to two numbers.

BETWEEN_KILLS_S.note: Time from one kill to the next fight starting. About 11% of the shortest seconds_per_kill (54 s, Rust Rat Runt).

KNOCKOUT_RESPAWN_S.gdd: Section 1: 'a knockout (60-second respawn, then the queue resumes)'; section 6: 'A knockout respawns in 60 seconds and resumes the queue'.

REFERENCE_RATION_TRIGGER_HP_FRACTION.gdd: Section 6: 'triggers ("eat a Ration below 40% HP")'; section 7, first session step 5, the same trigger. The player may set others; 0.4 is the reference.

HP_BASE.note: Revision 1's 90, scaled x10 (units.HP_DAMAGE_SCALE, settled). The base value itself is still a proposal.

HP_PER_VITALITY.note: Revision 1's 10, scaled x10. Vitality 1 gives 1,000 HP.

DAMAGE_PER_STYLE_LEVEL.note: Each style level adds this to the max hit before multipliers. Revision 1 added the style level itself (1 per level); x10 scaling makes it 10. weapon.power is stated in the same scaled units.

PRESSURE_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL.note: +1% max hit per Pressure level, every style. A multiplier, so unscaled.

HIT_CHANCE_BASE.note: Player hit chance when accuracy equals the monster's evasion.

ARMOUR_HALF_POINT.note: Armour 100 halves damage taken. Armour is Fortitude level plus the armour piece's armour points, not HP, so it is not scaled.

WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER.note: A matched style's max hit is multiplied by this. The band consequence of 1.25 under a one-style player is settled (see weakness); the value itself rests on that acceptance.

REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL.note: A reference player loses a quarter of their HP per at-level kill. Without Rations that is a knockout about every 4 kills.

BOSS_TARGET_WIN_CHANCE.gdd: Section 7: 'she beats Scrapjaw on her second attempt'. With win chance P, expected attempts to the first win are 1/P; 1/P = 2 gives P = 0.5.

BOSS_RATION_CAP_PER_ATTEMPT.gdd: Section 6: 'A boss fight allows at most 3 Rations.'

MAIN_COMBAT_SKILL_SHARE.gdd: content/tuning/xp-curve.json assumptions.MAIN_COMBAT_SKILL_SHARE. Which skill takes it is settled (combat_xp_split).

RATION_HEAL_HP.settled: Work order 012, 'Settled after review' (22 October 2026): 'The Ration heal is settled at 600.'
RATION_HEAL_HP.note: Settled in revision 6. Work order 012 (revision 5) kept 600 as the heal of the Rustmoor Ration, the only Ration item; it was provisional in revisions 1 to 4 (work order 009: 'How much a Ration heals is for the Cooking work order, within the model's rules'). No monster changes. x10 units. Chosen within rations.needs for the reference player at levels 1 to 20 against Rustmoor-level monsters: the hard rule (heal > reference monster_dps * PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S) needs more than 15.6, set by the Rust Rat Runt (0.25 * 1000 / 48 * 3); the soft rule (heal <= (1 - REFERENCE_RATION_TRIGGER_HP_FRACTION) * max_hp) allows at most 600, set by the smallest reference max HP in the band (1000 at level 1). 600 is the largest heal that never overheals at the 40% trigger anywhere in the band.

CALIBRATION_STEP.note: How much one calibration level raises a gear stat. Left to the calibration work order (work order 009, 'Settled after the first draft': 'The calibration step is left to the calibration work order').

skills._note: Section 6, Skills table: Vitality 'Hit points'; Pressure 'Steam-driven force'; Precision 'Accuracy and crits'; Melee 'Close damage'; Marksmanship 'Ranged damage'; Aetherics 'Storm and steam magic'; Fortitude 'Defence'. Which skill feeds which stat is derived from that table; every formula and coefficient is a proposal.

precision.formula: adds precision to accuracy; crit_chance = min(CRIT_CHANCE_CAP, CRIT_CHANCE_PER_PRECISION * precision)

melee.stat: style level when the weapon's style is melee

marksmanship.stat: style level when the weapon's style is marksmanship

aetherics.stat: style level when the weapon's style is aetherics

fortitude.formula: armour = fortitude + armour_piece.armour; damage_taken_mult = 1 - armour / (armour + ARMOUR_HALF_POINT)
fortitude.basis: proposal; one armour piece is settled (gear.loadout)

skills.styles_are_symmetric: The three style skills use identical formulas; they differ only through weapons and monster weakness. Derived from section 6: 'no skill is cheaper to level than another' read together with 'loadouts matter'; the symmetry itself is a proposal.

player_formulas.max_hit: (weapon.power + DAMAGE_PER_STYLE_LEVEL * style_level) * pressure_mult * (WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER if weapon.style == monster.weakness else 1)
player_formulas.landed_hit_roll: modelled as uniform on [0, max_hit]; a crit multiplies the roll by CRIT_MULTIPLIER. The engine rolls whole numbers (units.whole_number_rolls)

gear._note: Shape only. Section 6: 'Gear has fixed stats per calibration level, so a +5 Brass Spanner is identical everywhere'; section 6 Skills table: 'Calibrating ... Gear +1 to +20'. Values come in work order 011.

loadout.rule: A loadout is exactly one weapon and one armour piece. Consumables (Rations, teas) are not loadout slots; they are set by triggers.

consumables.settled: Work order 009, settled with revision 2: 'Consumables are set by triggers, not loadout slots. GDD section 7's calming tea is a trigger.'

loadout.gdd: Section 6: 'A loadout is one weapon and one armour piece, and its focus is the weapon's style: Melee, Marksmanship or Aetherics.'

fields.style: melee | marksmanship | aetherics (section 6: 'Monsters are weak to Melee, Marksmanship, or Aetherics')
fields.level_required: style level needed to equip (work order 008 carried forward: 'Scrapjaw's Cleaver needs level 20 to equip')
fields.stats_by_calibration: exactly 21 rows, +0 to +20, each {calibration, power, accuracy}; power in x10 units (units.HP_DAMAGE_SCALE); fixed, no rolls (derived from section 6)

power_at_plus_0.settled: Work order 011, 'Settled after the first draft' (22 October 2026): 'Weapon power at +0 is 10 x level required.'

scrapjaws_cleaver.settled: Work order 011, 'Settled after the first draft': 'Scrapjaw's Cleaver has +0 power 180, between the Steel Blade and the level-20 rule, so level-20 Cinderworks weapons outclass it.' The one exception to power_at_plus_0.

weapon.proposed_row_rule: power(c) = round(power(0) * (1 + CALIBRATION_STEP * c)), accuracy(c) = accuracy(0) + c
weapon.basis: proposal, except power_at_plus_0 and scrapjaws_cleaver (settled); CALIBRATION_STEP is left to the calibration work order

armour.slot: None. There is one armour slot (gear.loadout, settled), so coats, goggles and plate (section 6 Skills table: Tailoring, Smithing) all fill it and one is worn at a time.

armour_at_plus_0.settled: Work order 028 (29 October 2026): Jeremy settled armour points at +0 as 3 x the Fortitude level required to wear the piece.

armour.basis: proposal for the fields, except armour_at_plus_0 (settled); the single slot is settled

gear.reference_gear: For the target, 'the gear the zone offers' is the best +0 weapon of the matched style, and the best +0 armour piece, that the zone offers with level_required at or below the player's level. Calibration is headroom above the target, not part of it (proposal; section 7 month three treats calibrating toward +10 as a long sink). A boss listed in boss.reference_weapon is the one exception: its reference player holds that weapon instead of the best one (revision 8, work order 025).

monster_stats_shape._note: Fields work order 011 will set per monster. No values here. hp and max_hit are in x10 units (units.HP_DAMAGE_SCALE).

fields.max_hit: monster hits are modelled as uniform on [0, max_hit * damage_taken_mult]; the engine rolls whole numbers

attack_interval_rule.settled: Work order 011, 'Settled after the first draft' (22 October 2026): 'A monster's attack interval scales with its kill time: attack_interval_s = seconds_per_kill / 18, so every fight has about the same number of monster swings and harder monsters hit harder.' 'Settled after the inspector's review': 'Scrapjaw keeps the /18 attack interval' (270 / 18 = 15.0 s).

reference_player._note: The 'player at a monster's level' in the work order's constraint. Main style skill at L (the monster's weakness, so the loadout is matched); the other six combat skills at secondary_level(L); reference_gear for that level. max_hp is in x10 units.
reference_player.secondary_level: the highest level S with total_xp(S) <= total_xp(L) * OTHER_COMBAT_SKILLS_SHARE_EACH / MAIN_COMBAT_SKILL_SHARE, using the xp-curve table

weakness.rule: A weapon whose style equals monster.weakness multiplies max_hit by WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER. Unmatched weapons take no penalty beyond missing the bonus.
weakness.consequence: With Rations stocked, computed fight time scales inversely with the player's DPS, so the reference player's unmatched computed seconds per kill = BETWEEN_KILLS_S + WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER * (seconds_per_kill - BETWEEN_KILLS_S). Tinplate: 162 s matched, 201 s unmatched. The kill-time floor does not bind on an unmatched at-level fight, since it is already slower than seconds_per_kill.

single_style_band.settled: Work order 009: 'The band assumes a one-style player, who fights some Rustmoor rats unmatched. Rustmoor's 14.7 to 15.2 days are accepted.'
single_style_band.detail: Rustmoor's rat weaknesses rotate melee, marksmanship, aetherics, melee (Scrapjaw, melee, is a boss and not in the band). Holding seconds_per_kill fixed at level and taking the best target per five-level range, the band takes at most 14.68 days for melee, 14.83 marksmanship, 15.19 aetherics at WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER 1.25, against 13.96 if every target were matched.
single_style_band.scrapjaw_never_counted: The 14.68 / 14.83 / 15.19-day figures never counted Scrapjaw, before or after its weakness moved to melee (work order 011). They come from the four rats alone over the ranges 1-4, 5-9, 10-14 and 15-19; Scrapjaw is level 20, outside every range, and a boss is never a pacing target (pacing check: '1 boss(es), never counted'). Recomputed in work order 012 from the four rats and the xp-curve table, they reproduce exactly.

kill_time._note: Closed form, expected values, no simulation. seconds_per_kill in the monster files is the full cycle used by the pacing check (xp / seconds_per_kill), so it includes the time between kills and eating. Every HP and damage quantity below is in x10 units; every time is in seconds and unchanged by the scale.
kill_time.ration_drag: f = monster_dps * PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S / ration.heal_hp  (eating costs one player swing while the monster keeps attacking); requires f < 1

unstocked.assumptions: No HP regeneration between kills; a knockout restores full HP after the respawn; the half-fought monster is lost, costing on average half a fight (an approximation).

floor.formula: expected_seconds_per_kill = max(monster.seconds_per_kill, computed_seconds_per_kill), at every player level
floor.gdd: Section 6: 'A Tinker who outlevels a monster still takes its usual time per kill, so fighting easy monsters is safe but no faster; the reward for levelling is reaching harder ones.' Work order 009, settled with revision 2: 'The kill-time floor applies at every level, not only at or above the monster's level. Nothing kills faster than its target time.'
floor.rewards: XP, Crowns, drop rolls and the Ledger Page counter are paid per kill, unchanged, at the paced rate: per hour = 3600 / expected_seconds_per_kill times the per-kill amount. A floored fight therefore never pays faster than monster.xp * 3600 / monster.seconds_per_kill, so the pacing and drops checks that use seconds_per_kill stay valid.
floor.what_outlevelling_buys: Inside the floor, a stronger player takes less damage per kill: fewer Rations (rations_per_kill falls with t_fight computed unfloored) and fewer knockouts.

damage_and_rations.rule: Damage taken, Rations eaten and knockouts are computed from the unfloored fight; the extra floored seconds are idle and cost no HP.
damage_and_rations.settled: Work order 009, settled with revision 2: 'Damage taken and Rations eaten come from the unfloored fight; the extra floored seconds are idle.'

kill_time.target: For the reference player at monster.level with a matched reference_gear loadout and Rations stocked, computed_seconds_per_kill == monster.seconds_per_kill and monster_dps * t_fight == REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL * max_hp.
kill_time.solving_for_011: Pick evasion (suggested: equal to the reference accuracy, so the reference hit chance is HIT_CHANCE_BASE), hit_chance and attack_interval_s; then monster_dps = REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL * max_hp / (seconds_per_kill - BETWEEN_KILLS_S) fixes max_hit, and hp = player_dps * (seconds_per_kill - BETWEEN_KILLS_S) * (1 - f) fixes hp, rounded to a whole number.

rations._note: Section 6 ('eat a Ration below 40% HP') and the Skills table (Cooking produces 'Healing rations') name Rations. Since revision 5 one Ration item exists, item.rustmoor.rustmoor_ration (work order 012), healing RATION_HEAL_HP. Below is what the model needs from any Ration.

needs.heal_hp: a fixed whole number per Ration item, in x10 units (work order 009, 'Settled after the first draft': 'How much a Ration heals is for the Cooking work order, within the model's rules'). Settled at 600 for the Rustmoor Ration (constants.RATION_HEAL_HP; work order 012, 'Settled after review': 'The Ration heal is settled at 600.'): it meets hard_rule against every Rustmoor monster and is the largest heal that meets soft_rule at every reference level 1 to 20.
needs.hard_rule: heal_hp > monster_dps * PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S for any monster it is meant for, or the stocked formula diverges
needs.soft_rule: heal_hp <= (1 - REFERENCE_RATION_TRIGGER_HP_FRACTION) * max_hp of the reference player at the Ration's tier, so eating at the trigger never overheals
needs.consumption: rations_per_kill = monster_dps * t_fight / heal_hp (kill_time.stocked.rations_per_kill); at the reference, where kill_time.target gives monster_dps * t_fight == REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL * max_hp, that is REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL * max_hp / heal_hp, with no further division by (1 - f). This is Cooking's demand per kill
needs.boss_cap: At most BOSS_RATION_CAP_PER_ATTEMPT (3) per boss attempt (settled).

rations.reference_use: At the reference with heal 600, from kill_time.stocked.rations_per_kill as the combat and drops checks compute it (drops check, Crown sink report, revision 7): 0.416, 0.458, 0.542, 0.583 Rations per kill and 27.72, 15.28, 12.04, 9.72 Rations an hour against the Runt, Scrounger, Tinplate and Gaffer; 2,085 Rations over the 1 to 20 band.
rations.correction: Revision 7 (work order 013): rations.needs.consumption divided by (1 - f) on top of t_fight, which already carries the 1 / (1 - f) of kill_time.stocked.t_fight, so it counted the eating drag twice. It now agrees with kill_time.stocked.rations_per_kill, the formula the combat and drops checks use. reference_use was computed with the old formula (0.428, 0.465, 0.547, 0.588 a kill; 28.5, 15.5, 12.2, 9.8 an hour; 2,110 over the band) and is restated. No constant, monster or check result changes.
rations.basis: proposal for the rules (work order 012); heal_hp settled at 600 (work order 012, 'Settled after review'); boss cap settled

boss._note: Section 6: 'a boss attempt is a separate queue item, and a lost fight spends the attempt and pays no XP'. A boss fight is a race between two times, each approximated as normal (renewal central limit), so win chance is closed form.
boss.player_time: m_p = PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S * boss.hp / mean_swing_damage + n * PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S, where n = BOSS_RATION_CAP_PER_ATTEMPT if Rations are stocked else 0 (assumes every allowed Ration is eaten)
boss.player_time_variance: v_p = PLAYER_ATTACK_INTERVAL_S^2 * boss.hp * var_swing / mean_swing_damage^3, var_swing = second_moment - mean^2
boss.boss_time: m_b = boss.attack_interval_s * pool / boss_mean_swing, pool = max_hp + n * ration.heal_hp
boss.win_chance: P = Phi((m_b - m_p) / sqrt(v_p + v_b)), Phi the standard normal CDF. Every term in the ratio is a time, so the x10 scale leaves P unchanged.
boss.target: For the reference player at boss.level with a matched loadout and n Rations, m_b == m_p (so P == BOSS_TARGET_WIN_CHANCE) and BETWEEN_KILLS_S + m_p == boss.seconds_per_kill.

reference_weapon._note: Work order 025, Jeremy's decision after part 1 (28 October 2026): a launch-day player cannot be assumed to buy a Steel Blade on the Exchange by day 13, so Scrapjaw is tuned to the weapon a player actually holds. A boss listed here is solved for a reference player who holds this weapon at +0 in place of gear.reference_gear's best weakness-style weapon; level, the other six skills (reference_player), armour and Rations are unchanged. A boss not listed keeps gear.reference_gear.

monster.rustmoor.scrapjaw.why: Work order 025 option (c): 'The reference player holds the power-100 hammer, and Scrapjaw's stats come down so that player wins half the time at melee 20.' The Riveting Hammer (melee, level_required 10, power 100) is the best melee weapon the Act I walk ever holds before the fight: work order 025 part 1 measured it made on day 15.54, 14.54 and 12.96 at 2, 3 and 4 check-ins, and the Steel Blade never, since forge_steel_blade needs Smithing 15 and the walk ends Act I at Smithing 10.
monster.rustmoor.scrapjaw.hp_derivation: derived: boss.target with the hammer. At level 20 with the other skills at 6, accuracy 26 equals Scrapjaw's evasion 26, so hit chance 0.75; max_hit (100 + 10 x 20) x 1.06 x 1.25 = 397.5; crit 0.03; mean swing 0.75 x 198.75 x 1.015 = 151.30. BETWEEN_KILLS_S + m_p = 270 gives hp = (270 - 6 - 3 x 3) x 151.30 / 3 = 12,860.4, so 12,860. Revision 7's 15,004 is the same solve with the Steel Blade (mean 176.51, 15,003.8). Every other Scrapjaw stat is unchanged, so m_b is unchanged and m_b == m_p still holds: win chance 0.500, won attempt 270.0 s.

boss.expected_attempt_seconds: BETWEEN_KILLS_S + m_p + (1 - P) * KNOCKOUT_RESPAWN_S (approximation: a lost fight is counted at full length, then a knockout). At any player level, a won attempt takes no less than boss.seconds_per_kill (kill_time.floor).

steepness.settled: Work order 011, 'Settled after the inspector's review' (22 October 2026), replacing work order 009's 15 points and 4%: 'The settled steepness is now about 9 points of win chance per level and about 15% with the wrong style.'
steepness.figures: Revision 8 (work order 025): Scrapjaw (weak to melee, hp 12,860), reference player with the Riveting Hammer (+0, power 100; boss.reference_weapon), 3 Rations, RATION_HEAL_HP 600: win chance 0.397 at level 19, 0.500 at 20, 0.596 at 21 (-10.3 and +9.6 points); 0.152 with the wrong style at level 20 and the same power (Steel Carbine or Spark Rod, power 100), 0.383 with the best wrong-style weapon (Garnet Rifle or Garnet Rod, power 150); 0.001 without Rations. Other melee weapons at level 20: Iron Crowbar 0.204, Steel Blade 0.728, Scrapjaw's Cleaver 0.816. The reference player's other six skills are 6 at levels 19 to 21, so only the main style moves. Revision 7, with the Steel Blade and hp 15,004: 0.405, 0.500, 0.589; 0.152 wrong style (power 150); 0.001 without Rations.
steepness.revision_8_settled: Jeremy accepted the revision 8 curve on 28 October 2026 (work order 025): -10.3 and +9.6 points per level around 20, 0.152 with the wrong style at equal power, 0.383 with the best wrong-style weapon in Rustmoor (power 150), and 0.728 with the Steel Blade.

boss.basis: proposal, except BOSS_TARGET_WIN_CHANCE (derived), the Ration cap and the accepted steepness (settled)

combat_xp_split.rule: Each kill's combat XP goes MAIN_COMBAT_SKILL_SHARE (70%) to the loadout's focus, which is the style skill of the weapon (Melee, Marksmanship or Aetherics), and OTHER_COMBAT_SKILLS_SHARE_EACH (5%) to each of the other six combat skills. Vitality, Fortitude, Pressure and Precision can never be the focus and always take the 5% share.
combat_xp_split.gdd: Section 6: 'its focus is the weapon's style: Melee, Marksmanship or Aetherics'; work order 009: 'Only the three attack styles can be a loadout's focus. Vitality, Fortitude, Pressure and Precision always take the 5% share.'
combat_xp_split.why: The curve's base, its day-2 check (total level passes 50 only at 70/5 with three crafting skills) and the Ledger Page counter (work order 008) all rest on 70/5.
consequences: Vitality and Fortitude sit at 6, 10 and 18 when the main skill reaches 20, 45 and 70 (reference_player table): max HP 1,500, 1,900, 2,700; damage taken cut by 5.7%, 9.1%, 15.3%.

Vitality and Fortitude do not change at-level kill time. They change Ration use, knockouts without Rations, and boss odds: at Scrapjaw (melee reference player, Riveting Hammer since revision 8, 3 Rations, RATION_HEAL_HP 600; the same figures as revision 7's Steel Blade), +5 Vitality (max HP 1,500 to 2,000) takes the win chance from 50% to 73%, +5 Fortitude (armour 6 to 11) to 58%.
A player who switches styles to match every weakness splits the 70% across up to three styles and levels each more slowly than the curve assumes.
Story checks on Vitality, Fortitude, Pressure or Precision cannot assume more than about 6 in Act I, 10 in Act II, 18 in Act III.

Damage taken and Rations eaten from the unfloored fight (kill_time.floor.damage_and_rations)
Consumables set by triggers, not loadout slots (gear.loadout.consumables)
Checks use the closed forms as written, continuous moments (units.closed_forms_for_checks)
One-style band assumption and Rustmoor's 14.7 to 15.2 days (weakness.single_style_band)
Boss steepness: about 9 points per level, about 15% with the wrong style (boss.steepness; work order 011)
Monster attack interval is seconds_per_kill / 18 (monster_stats_shape.attack_interval_rule; work order 011)
Weapon power at +0 is 10 x level_required (gear.weapon.power_at_plus_0; work order 011)
Scrapjaw's Cleaver has +0 power 180 (gear.weapon.scrapjaws_cleaver; work order 011)
Ration heal 600, the Rustmoor Ration (constants.RATION_HEAL_HP; work order 012, 'Settled after review')
Focus is one of the three attack styles (combat_xp_split)
Loadout is one weapon and one armour piece (gear.loadout)
Hit points and damage scaled x10 (units)
Calibration step left to the calibration work order (constants.CALIBRATION_STEP)
Armour points at +0 are 3 x the Fortitude level required to wear the piece (gear.armour.armour_at_plus_0; work order 028, 29 October 2026)
open_questions: CALIBRATION_STEP: for the calibration work order.
Every value still marked proposal (intervals, HP base and per-Vitality, hit and crit constants, ARMOUR_HALF_POINT, WEAKNESS_MULTIPLIER, REFERENCE_DAMAGE_SHARE_PER_KILL) waits on Jeremy.
